title: Identification of Diatraea spp Based on Cytochrome Oxidase II and SSCP
author: Gloria Patricia Barrera
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ipqcdmw
materials: Dissection, DNA extraction and COII fragment amplification: Abdomens from insects must be dissected and maintained in ethanol at 70 % v/v in sterile distilled water to DNA extractions. DNA of insects must be obtained from complete abdomen by using commercial kit (DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit, QIAGEN) and quantified by spectrophotometry (Nanodrop 1000, Thermo-Fisher). COII amplification: In vitro amplifications of CO II fragments must be carried out by the Polymerase Chain Reaction method (PCR) in standard conditions (final volume 25 μL) using Taq polymerase (PROMEGA), 50 ng of template and the primers previously described and used in Diatraea: A-298 (5’- ATTGGACATCAATGATATTGA-3’) and B-tLYS (5’ GTTTAAGAGACCAGTACTTG-3’) (Simon et al. 1994; Lange et al. 2004, Palacio et al. 2010). Thermal cycling was performed using the following conditions: 1 cycle at 95 °C for 3 min; 34 cycles at 95 °C for 10 s; 53 °C for 45 s, and 72 °C for 30 s; and one cycle at 72 °C for 5 min. Aliquots of amplification products were resolved in 1% w/v agarose gel electrophoresis and later stained with SYBR-Safe (Invitrogen). Amplicons will be used for SSCP methodology.

Preparing electrophoresis equipment For this protocol the Biorad Sequi-Gen® GT (38 x 50 cm) was used. The detailed instructions for assembly are in http://www.cmu.edu.cn/cmu/upl_files/327/2007111485016635.pdf To prepare Sequi-gen glass plate (IPC) and outer plates follow the Biorad manual instructions. Additionally, after cleaning, add silicone and shine the IPC (rub until silicone residue is completely removed). The outer plate must be prepared with bind silane (See: Reagent Preparation) and after cleaned two times with ethanol. Note: Tips and paper towels used for the treatment of outer plate should be discarded immediately after use avoiding contamination of IPC. Assembly the glass plate sandwich and slowly inject the polyacrylamide solution (6%, 49:1) with a 100 mL syringe avoiding bubbles formation. To prepare polyacrylamide solution and electrophoresis buffers see Reagent Preparation.

Dissection, DNA extraction and COII fragment amplification: Abdomens from insects must be dissected and maintained in ethanol at 70 % v/v in sterile distilled water to DNA extractions. DNA of insects must be obtained from complete abdomen by using commercial kit (DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit, QIAGEN) and quantified by spectrophotometry (Nanodrop 1000, Thermo-Fisher). COII amplification: In vitro amplifications of CO II fragments must be carried out by the Polymerase Chain Reaction method (PCR) in standard conditions (final volume 25 μL) using Taq polymerase (PROMEGA), 50 ng of template and the primers previously described and used in Diatraea: A-298 (5’- ATTGGACATCAATGATATTGA-3’) and B-tLYS (5’ GTTTAAGAGACCAGTACTTG-3’) (Simon et al. 1994; Lange et al. 2004, Palacio et al. 2010). Thermal cycling was performed using the following conditions: 1 cycle at 95 °C for 3 min; 34 cycles at 95 °C for 10 s; 53 °C for 45 s, and 72 °C for 30 s; and one cycle at 72 °C for 5 min. Aliquots of amplification products were resolved in 1% w/v agarose gel electrophoresis and later stained with SYBR-Safe (Invitrogen). Amplicons will be used for SSCP methodology.

steps.title: Prepare bind‑silane coating
steps.instruction: Mix absolute ethanol (95 %), glacial acetic acid (5 %) and Bind‑Silane (0.13 %) to make a coating solution; apply 1 mL to the outer glass surfaces of the gel plates and let dry.

steps.title: Make 10X TBE buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve Tris base (53.85 g), Boric acid (27.51 g) and 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0, 20 mL) in distilled water and bring the final volume to 500 mL.

steps.title: Prepare 40 % acrylamide/bisacrylamide stock
steps.instruction: Combine acrylamide (39.2 g) and bisacrylamide (0.8 g) with distilled water and adjust the solution to a final volume of 100 mL (49:1 ratio, 40 % total monomer).

steps.title: Prepare 6 % polyacrylamide gel solution
steps.instruction: In a clean container mix 15 mL of the 40 % acrylamide/bisacrylamide stock, 10 mL of 10X TBE buffer and 75 mL distilled water to a total of 100 mL; immediately add ammonium persulfate (850 µL of 10 % APS) and TEMED (108 µL), then pour the solution into the bind‑silane‑coated gel plates and allow polymerization.

steps.title: Prepare loading buffer
steps.instruction: Combine formamide (95 % v/v), EDTA (20 mM), bromophenol blue (0.05 % w/v) and Xylene‑cyanol (0.05 % w/v) in distilled water to make the loading buffer; keep on ice.

steps.title: Mix PCR product with loading buffer and denature
steps.instruction: Add 9 µL loading buffer to 1 µL COII PCR product, vortex briefly, then denature at 95 °C for 5 min and immediately chill on ice for 3 min.

steps.title: Load samples and run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Load approximately 1.3 µL of the denatured mixture into each well, place the electrode caps, connect the power supply, apply 600 V and run the gel for 8 h.

steps.title: Fix gel
steps.instruction: Prepare fixation solution by mixing absolute ethanol (150 mL), glacial acetic acid (15 mL) and distilled water to 1500 mL (10 % v/v ethanol, 1 % v/v acetic acid). Immerse the gel in this solution for 3 min, then wash the gel with distilled water for 3 min.

steps.title: Oxidize gel
steps.instruction: Prepare oxidation solution by mixing nitric acid (22.5 mL) with distilled water to a final volume of 1500 mL (1.5 % v/v nitric acid). Incubate the gel in this solution for 3 min, then wash with distilled water for 3 min.

steps.title: Stain gel with silver nitrate
steps.instruction: Prepare nitrate (staining) solution by dissolving silver nitrate (1.5 g) and formaldehyde (1.8 mL) in distilled water to 1500 mL (0.1 % w/v AgNO₃, 0.045 % v/v formaldehyde). Incubate the gel in this solution for 20 min, then rinse briefly with distilled water for 10 s.

steps.title: Develop gel (reveal)
steps.instruction: Prepare reveal solution by dissolving sodium carbonate (30 g) and formaldehyde (540 µL) in distilled water to 1000 mL (3 % w/v Na₂CO₃, 0.02 % v/v formaldehyde). Place the gel in this solution and allow bands to appear (≈5 min).

steps.title: Stop staining reaction
steps.instruction: Prepare stop solution by mixing glacial acetic acid (75 mL) with distilled water to 1500 mL (5 % v/v acetic acid). Add this solution to the gel, leave for 4 min, then wash the gel with distilled water for 4 min.
